monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity significantly this month, shifting time into Zones 3–4 and improving pace, but at the cost of reduced volume and aerobic efficiency stability.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3 time jumped from 36% to 32% and Zone 4 from 12% to 21% — a sharp 9-percentage-point increase in high-intensity work, while Z2 dropped from 47% to 30%, indicating a meaningful shift away from foundational aerobic development.

goal_tracker.message: You need 7.6 more km across 2 remaining sessions (e.g., two 3.8–4.0 km runs) to match last month’s distance total.

insights.title: Efficiency improved modestly despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.44 m/sec per bpm — a positive sign that your stride is becoming slightly more economical even as average HR increased by 6 bpm and pace improved by 28 sec/km.

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 3–4 at expense of Zone 2 base-building
insights.body: Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 30% of total HR time, while Zones 3+4 now comprise 53% — well above the 40–45% recommended for sustainable aerobic development in recreational runners with <5 years experience.

insights.title: Stride length variability correlates with effort level
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 70.96 cm (6.2 km @ 9:00/km, HR 142) to 90.77 cm (5.0 km @ 7:25/km, HR 163), showing strong neuromuscular adaptation under load — but vertical oscillation remained stable (7.8–8.4 cm), suggesting form integrity is holding.

insights.title: Aerobic TE rose +0.4 but recovery metrics show strain
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE increased to 3.4, yet ground contact time rose from 306–307 ms (harder efforts) to 314 ms (recovery run on 4/17), and cadence dipped to 149 spm — early signs of accumulated fatigue affecting neuromuscular readiness.

recommendations.action: Replace your next scheduled run with a 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR ≤138 bpm, pace ~9:15–9:45/km) focused solely on relaxed breathing and cadence consistency at 152 spm.
recommendations.reason: Zone 2 volume has dropped sharply (30% vs 47% last month), and your 4/17 run showed elevated ground contact (+7 ms vs hardest effort) and lower cadence — signaling need for active recovery and aerobic reconnection.

recommendations.action: Add 3 × 30-second strides at 4:30/km pace after your next easy run, focusing on landing midfoot and minimizing vertical oscillation (target <7.5 cm based on current 7.8–8.4 cm range).
recommendations.reason: Your best pace (445 sec/km = 7:25/km) occurred at high stride length (90.77 cm) and elevated VO2 max (34.0 → 35.0), suggesting neuromuscular potential — but vertical oscillation remains a limiting efficiency factor.

recommendations.action: Perform a 5-minute post-run mobility routine targeting hip flexors and calves immediately after your next two runs, given ground contact time increased to 311–314 ms on easier efforts — a sign of reduced leg spring efficiency.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time rose on lower-intensity runs (311–314 ms) versus harder ones (306–307 ms), which is atypical and suggests emerging stiffness or fatigue in elastic recoil capacity.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild Zone 2 endurance foundation while restoring neuromuscular springiness and stride efficiency — prioritizing rhythm, relaxation, and tissue resilience over pace or distance.
suggested_sessions: 30-min walk + mobility routine (hip flexors, calves, plantar fascia)
